record.paper_title: Open Problems in Heavy Quarkonium Physics
record.original_question: How should the ground-state bottomonium hyperfine splitting be determined once next-to-next-to-leading-order effects are included, and what value should be expected experimentally? The paper notes that no experimental data were yet available for bottomonium hyperfine splittings and that NNLO effects are potentially important because both non-perturbative contributions, relevant when ΛQCD is of order E, and mass-correction effects first enter at that order. The open problem is to produce a quantitatively reliable prediction, including these corrections, and confront it with measurement.

evidence.quote: In the bottomonium case there are not yet experimental data.
We note, however, that NNLO corrections may be potentially important for this observable, also considering that at this order new type of corrections will appear for the first time:
• non-perturbative corrections, which are parametrically of NNLO in the situation ΛQCD ∼ E.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In non-relativistic QCD, consider the ground-state bottomonium system consisting of the spin-triplet vector meson Υ(1S) and the spin-singlet pseudoscalar meson η_b(1S), formed from a b-quark and its antiquark. The 1S hyperfine splitting is defined as ΔE_hf(1S) = M_Υ(1S) − M_η_b(1S).

(a) Derive a quantitatively reliable theoretical prediction of ΔE_hf(1S) that consistently includes next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) corrections in the perturbative expansion of weak-coupling non-relativistic QCD. In particular, the prediction must incorporate, at NNLO, both:
  (i) non-perturbative contributions, which are parametrically of NNLO in the regime where the QCD scale Λ_QCD is of the order of the typical binding energy E of the bound state; and
  (ii) heavy-quark mass-correction effects, which first enter at this order.

(b) Provide the expected experimental value of ΔE_hf(1S) for the 1S bottomonium system and compare it to the NNLO theoretical prediction obtained in part (a), assessing the agreement within the combined theoretical and experimental uncertainties.
artifact.status_search_result: Since the original posing of the problem, η_b(1S) was discovered experimentally (BaBar, 2008), making the 1S bottomonium hyperfine splitting measurable; the current experimental value is approximately 60 MeV. Theoretical NNLO/NRQCD continuum predictions (e.g., 52.9 ± 5.5 MeV) and lattice QCD calculations (e.g., 57.5(2.3)(1.0) MeV, 60.0(6.4) MeV) are now available and broadly compatible with experiment, though uncertainties from non-perturbative and higher-order effects remain a subject of ongoing study. Thus the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Bottomonium Hyperfine Splitting on the Lattice and in the Continuum
status_evidence.snippet: M_Υ(1S) - M_η_b(1S) = 52.9 ± 5.5 MeV from a semianalytic continuum approach using NRQCD with high-order radiative corrections.
status_evidence.claim: NNLO-level continuum prediction of the 1S bottomonium hyperfine splitting now exists.

status_evidence.title: Bottomonium hyperfine splittings from lattice NRQCD including radiative and relativistic corrections
status_evidence.snippet: M(Upsilon,1S) - M(eta_b,1S) = 60.0(6.4) MeV from lattice NRQCD including radiative and relativistic corrections.
status_evidence.claim: Lattice NRQCD now provides predictions including relativistic and radiative corrections.

status_evidence.title: Bottomonium precision tests from full lattice QCD
status_evidence.snippet: M_Υ - M_η_b = 57.5(2.3)(1.0) MeV from full lattice QCD with HISQ.
status_evidence.claim: Recent full lattice QCD gives a precise prediction in agreement with experiment.

status_evidence.title: Searching high and low for bottomonium
status_evidence.snippet: Report of the discovery of η_b(1S) by BaBar.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental observation of η_b(1S) has been achieved, enabling measurement of the splitting.
